findings.rationale: AI-project check paths return success from a lexical heuristic/summary without calling parse_ai_project. Unterminated blocks, duplicate declarations, and invalid component bodies can therefore be reported as successfully analyzed by both native and browser check entrypoints.

AiProjectSummary stores only one component and one unkeyed set of contract fields. Each ai_component overwrites the name while omitted fields retain values from the preceding component, so --component cannot select earlier components and replay may validate one component using another component's contract.

A relative dataset source declared in the project is converted directly to PathBuf and read relative to the process working directory. Invoking fslc from outside the project directory therefore reads the wrong file or fails; the path should be resolved relative to the project file.

Document checking accepts V2 approval records and exposes their signature key IDs without verifying their signatures or trust roots. A forged or untrusted signed approval can consequently be incorporated into the expected rendered document and accepted as conformant.

Generation renders an AppliedApproval with target.reviewed_digest, but document check reconstructs the same overlay using target.digest. When a conforming reviewed artifact differs byte-for-byte from the canonical rendering, a document produced by generate cannot be reproduced by check and is falsely reported drifted.

The approval check exit status is nonzero only for signature-invalid. Other unsuccessful evaluation statuses produced for changed specifications, artifacts, claim sets, or generator versions still exit 0, allowing a drifted approval to pass CI gates.

Migration contents are read and semantically validated during planning, but commit later renames replacements over each path without verifying that the file still has the planned contents or identity. Concurrent editor/process changes made in that interval are silently overwritten with a migration derived from stale input.

effect_request handling ignores the return value of BTreeSet::insert, so a repeated request for the same effect and correlation ID is silently collapsed. One subsequent completion can then yield a conformant result even though an irreversible external effect was requested multiple times.

After detecting an uncorrelated completion or a duplicate irreversible completion, replay continues into domain_replay_step and updates completed, pending, observed, and monitor state. Invalid log entries can therefore execute the modeled completion again and corrupt the state used to assess later entries and report final_state.

Literate materialization uses a predictable PID-derived sibling path and std::fs::write rather than exclusive creation. A pre-existing symlink at that name is followed and can cause an arbitrary writable target to be overwritten before the guard removes the sibling path.
